You are researching a live production codebase (read-only — do not modify anything) to build understanding for a design decision. Do NOT write any code or edit any files. This is pure research/reporting.

CONTEXT: Soul Pilates is a Pilates studio CRM (ASP.NET Core / .NET 10 backend, Astro 6 frontend with vanilla in-page JS, MongoDB). The source lives on a remote server, NOT on this local machine. Access it via SSH:

    ssh -i ~/.ssh/soulpilates_deploy root@51.79.226.200 "cat /path/to/file"

or to grep across the repo:

    ssh -i ~/.ssh/soulpilates_deploy root@51.79.226.200 "grep -rn 'pattern' /opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro"

The frontend lives at /opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro on that remote host. Plan on doing all reading through SSH command output — there's no local checkout.

YOUR FOCUS: the customer-facing booking flow and package/wallet display, specifically around private classes and any existing "make this a duo/2-person" option. I need exact, file:line-cited answers to:

1. **The public booking page** (`src/pages/booking.astro` or similar — find it) and its supporting script(s) — when a customer books a PRIVATE-format class, is there currently any UI control (checkbox/toggle/radio) letting them mark it as a 2-person ("Duo") booking? The business owner says this option currently exists at booking time with a price change (850,000 → 1,300,000 VND). Find the exact HTML/JS implementing this. Quote it. If you can't find it in `booking.astro`, check `checkout.astro`, any booking-widget component, or search the whole Astro tree for "1300000", "1,300,000", "850000", "850,000", "Duo", "duo", "2 person", "second person", "party size", "guest count".

2. Once found, trace how that "duo" selection is sent to the backend — what API call does it make (`POST /api/booking/reserve` with what extra field in the payload?), and does the backend (BookingController / SchedulingService, cross-reference with what the other research agents find) actually persist that as anything structured, or is it just a price override with no durable "this was a duo booking" marker? Quote the request payload construction in the frontend JS.

3. **`my-package.astro`** (the customer's own package/wallet view) — how are a client's `ClientPackage`s rendered? What fields are shown (format, credits remaining, expiry)? Is `Format` shown as a raw value like "PRIVATE" or translated to a friendlier label? This matters for figuring out how a "Duo Private" package would need to visually/textually distinguish itself from a regular "Private" package if they share the same underlying Format.

4. **Admin `client-profile.astro`** (admin panel client detail page) — same question for the staff-facing view of a client's packages/wallet — where in admin does staff see & manage a client's packages (any "grant package" UI, any package list rendering)?

5. **Admin `products.astro` / `product-form.astro`** — how does staff currently create a new sellable Product/package in the admin UI? What fields does the form expose (Type, Format, Credits, price, validity)? This tells us what the admin would need to fill in to formally create a "Duo Private" package product, and whether the form already supports picking a Format of PRIVATE with different credit/pricing.

6. **Admin `pos.astro`** — the point-of-sale screen — how does staff sell a package to a walk-in there? Does it list Products, and can they sell an ad-hoc/custom-priced item not in the catalog?

Report back structured with file:line citations and short verbatim code/HTML quotes. This report will be read by someone designing how to add a formal "Duo Private" package option to booking, checkout, and the client's profile — be precise about what UI/UX exists today vs. what's missing.

Public booking page — the "Duo" toggle EXISTS today (SPM-98) **File:** `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/booking.astro` HTML (booking offcanvas footer), lines 336–343: ```html ``` Visibility logic, lines 1590–1598 (only shown for `PRIVATE` format, empty slot): ```js const isPrivate = session.format === "PRIVATE"; const canDuo = isPrivate && !isFull && spotsLeft >= 1; duoCheckbox.checked = false; // reset each time the panel opens duoToggle.style.display = canDuo ? "flex" : "none"; ``` Carried into the checkout intent, lines 1722–1739: ```js const duoEl = document.getElementById("duoCheckbox"); const isDuo = !!duoEl && duoEl.checked && duoEl.closest("#duoToggle")?.style.display !== "none"; ... sessionStorage.setItem("sp_booking_intent", JSON.stringify({ ... duo: session.format === "PRIVATE" && isDuo, quantity: session.format === "PRIVATE" && isDuo ? 2 : 1, })); ``` `checkout.astro` reads that intent (line 2085–2086) and surfaces a read-only summary row/price note (lines 83–94, 152–160): ```html
Booking type
...>Duo Class · 2 people
``` ```js function isDuoBooking() { return session?.format === "PRIVATE" && intent?.duo === true; } ``` **Price:** 850,000 → 1,300,000 VND is confirmed and is a real, admin-configurable-in-principle (but currently only settable via DB/code, not surfaced in any admin UI) flat rate: - `SoulPilates.Migration/Commands/BlueprintSeedCommand.cs:401` — `DropInPrice = 850_000m` (the seeded PRIVATE class drop-in price). - `SoulPilates.Core/Entities/GlobalSettings.cs:116` — `public decimal PrivateDuoPrice { get; set; } = 1_300_000m;` with doc comment: *"Flat price for a PRIVATE Duo Class (2 people). When > 0, a private session booked for 2 bills this instead of 2x the drop-in. Cash/online only — credit bookings still cost 2 credits."* - `SoulPilates.Services/PaymentService.cs:143–146` — `DuoAwareTotal(format, dropIn, seats, privateDuoPrice)`: `if (format == "PRIVATE" && seats == 2 && privateDuoPrice > 0m) return privateDuoPrice;` Notably, `PrivateDuoPrice` is **not exposed** by `GET /api/payment/checkout-settings` (`PaymentController.cs:115-143`) and there is no `PrivateDuoPrice` input anywhere in `admin/settings.astro` (grep confirmed zero hits) — it's a server-only hardcoded default, invisible to admins in the UI. ### 2. How the "duo" flag reaches the backend — NOT a structured field, only inferred from quantity **Frontend payload, `checkout.astro:2568–2578`:** ```js const resBody = { sessionId, name, phone, email, goals: intent.goals || null, equipmentType: intent.equipmentType || null, quantity, marketingSource: localStorage.getItem("sp_mkt_source") || null, marketingDetail: localStorage.getItem("sp_mkt_detail") || null, promoCode: _claimedOffer ? _claimedOffer.code || null : null, offerType: _claimedOffer ? _claimedOffer.type || null : null, }; ``` There is **no `duo` key at all** — the entire "duo-ness" collapses to `quantity: 2`, sent via `POST /api/booking/reserve` (line 2583). **Backend, `SoulPilates.API/Controllers/BookingController.cs`:** `ReserveRequest` (line ~694) has `public int Quantity { get; set; } = 1;` — no `IsDuo`/`Duo` field exists on the DTO. The comment on it literally says *"Server-clamped to 1 for PRIVATE sessions"* as the general rule. **`SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs:1833` `ReserveSpotAsync`**, lines ~1876–1907, is where the duo case is special-cased: ```csharp // SPM-98 "Make it a Duo Class" — a PRIVATE session may be booked as a // duo (2 seats) by a single booker who covers both seats. We mirror the // existing DUO format (capacity 2): the booker's single attendance carries // Quantity=2, CurrentBookings is incremented by 2, and 2 credits / 2× the // drop-in are charged via the same multi-seat path GROUP bookings use. if (session.Format == "PRIVATE") { var othersBooked = session.CurrentBookings - (existingReserved?.Quantity ?? 0); if (quantity == 2 && othersBooked <= 0) { if (session.Capacity < 2) { /* bump session.Capacity to 2 */ } } else { quantity = 1; } } ``` **There is no durable "this was a duo booking" marker anywhere.** `Attendance.Quantity` (`SoulPilates.Core/Entities/Attendance.cs:77`) is the only signal — a PRIVATE-format attendance with `Quantity == 2` *is* the duo, inferred after the fact by re-checking `format == "PRIVATE" && seats == 2` (as `PaymentService.DuoAwareTotal` and `SchedulingService.cs:1164/1189` both do). No `IsDuo` boolean, no `BookingType` enum, nothing stored that says "this is a Duo Class" as opposed to "customer happened to book 2 seats of a session whose capacity was bumped to 2." If a future PRIVATE session legitimately had 2 unrelated people book 1 seat each (not possible today since capacity is 1 unless bumped by this exact code path, but worth flagging as a fragile inference), the marker would be ambiguous. Credit deduction for a duo booking on check-in also comes from a client's **PRIVATE**-format package (not a distinct "DUO" package) — `WalletService.GetActivePackagesForClientAsync(clientId, format)` (`WalletService.cs:73-92`) does exact-match on `ClientPackage.Format == session.Format`, and `session.Format` stays `"PRIVATE"` throughout the SPM-98 duo flow (only `Quantity`/`Capacity` change), so 2 credits are drawn from a regular Private package, not any duo-specific package. ### 3. `my-package.astro` — client wallet view **File:** `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/my-package.astro` - Format filter chips (lines 61–69) only offer **All / Group / Private** — no DUO chip exists: ```html

"#f59e0b" : "#6366f1"; ... ${escapeHtml(fmt)} ``` So today a client sees literally `PRIVATE` or `GROUP` as the tag text — no friendly label map exists here (unlike `admin/products.astro`, see #5). Tapping a tile calls `addToCart(product)` (lines 986–1003), which reads `p.basePrice` for pricing (line 990). - Class check-in/walk-in flows (`addClassToCart`, `addWalkInToCart`, `addCollectPaymentToCart`, lines 1030-1046, 1610-1676) carry a `_classFormat` (uppercased) alongside the session, used later to decide package/credit matching (SPM-124 comment, line 1629-1631). - **No ad-hoc/custom-priced catalog item exists.** The only "custom price" affordance found is a `prompt()` at line 1375, used solely when a *collect-payment* amount differs from the expected due — it asks for a mandatory reason, not for creating a new sellable line item. There's a generic discount row (`discountType` VND/PCT, lines 300-308) that can reduce a cart total, and a voucher/promo-code row (lines 311-338), but no "add arbitrary item at arbitrary price not in the product catalog" control. - Merchandise variants use a dedicated SKU/pack picker (`openVariantPicker`, `renderSockConfigurator`, lines 1750-2017) — again, all catalog-driven. **Conclusion for POS:** selling a "Duo Private" package to a walk-in today would work exactly like any other `PACKAGE` product — it would need to be created via `product-form.astro` (per #5) and would then simply appear as a `productGrid` tile in POS; there is no ability today to improvise a duo sale at a custom price outside the catalog. --- ## Summary for the design decision 1. A "Duo" concept **already exists in two disconnected forms**: - **(A) SPM-98 booking-time checkbox** — cosmetic-only opt-in on PRIVATE sessions at `booking.astro:336-343`/`1586-1598`/`1720-1739`, carried as `quantity: 2` (no `duo` field) to `POST /api/booking/reserve`, billed via a hardcoded `GlobalSettings.PrivateDuoPrice` (1,300,000 VND, `GlobalSettings.cs:116`) with **no admin UI to change it** and **no durable "was a duo" flag** on `Attendance` — just `Format == "PRIVATE" && Quantity == 2` inferred after the fact. - **(B) A genuine `DUO` class Format** — a full third format (alongside `GROUP`/`PRIVATE`) already wired through scheduling (`calendar.astro`, `classes.astro`, `instructor/schedule.astro`), Products (`product-form.astro`'s `pFormatDuo` option, `products.astro`'s `formatLabel` map), and wallet matching (`WalletService.GetActivePackagesForClientAsync` exact-matches `ClientPackage.Format`). This is what a formal "Duo Private" *package* would naturally hook into — but it requires the session itself to be scheduled with `Format = "DUO"`, which is a different code path from the SPM-98 checkbox that leaves `session.Format = "PRIVATE"`. 2. Gaps to close for a formal "Duo Private" package: `my-package.astro` has no `DUO` filter chip and shows raw/untranslated format text with no distinguishing color for `DUO` (falls into the generic indigo "Group" color bucket) — needs a label/translation and filter update. Admin `client-profile.astro` and `products.astro` are already fine (friendly names/labels). The SPM-98 checkbox and the DUO format are currently two unrelated mechanisms billing/crediting differently (flat settings price vs package credits by format) and reconciling/choosing between them (or formally connecting the checkbox to `DUO`-format products) is the core design question.
